utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could you call the case number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-01-47-T, the Prosecutor versus Enver Hadzihasanovic and Amir Kubura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we have the appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, Counsel. For the Prosecution, Chester Stamp and Ekkehard Withopf, and the case manager, Kimberly Fleming.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And the appearances for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Mr. President. Good day, Your Honours. My name is Edina Residovic, counsel; Stephane Bourgon, co-counsel; and our legal assistant, Muriel Cauvin, a lawyer from Paris, represent General Hadzihasanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And could the other Defence team represent itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Your Honours. Mr. Kubura is represented by Fahrudin Ibrisimovic, Mr. Rodney Dixon, and our legal assistant, Mr. Mulalic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The Trial Chamber would like to greet the Prosecution, the Defence, and the accused. We will resume the proceedings today, and we'll be hearing a witness. Before we hear this witness, I would like to inform everyone that next week a hearing has been scheduled for Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, and Friday morning. With regard to the hearings on Tuesday and Wednesday in Courtroom III, it's possible that these hearings might be held in this courtroom, in Courtroom II, since according to the schedule a hearing should be in Courtroom II which relates to another case. But as it appears that is there might be public people present and there are only four places in this gallery, we have to take this into account. We will have more details in the near future, but please bear this in mind. Next week on Tuesday and Wednesday, we might be back in this courtroom; whereas, according to the schedule, we should be in Courtroom III. Are there any comments to be made at this time by either of the parties before we have the witness called into the courtroom? No comments. Very well, then. Could the usher, who has disappeared - I think she's gone to look for the witness - I'm going to ask the usher to call the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, while we're awaiting the witness, may I just indicate to the Court that although the 65 ter summary in respect to the witness Kruno Rajic indicates, I think by some error, that it's going to be a half hour, he might take just a little bit longer than that. The time there clearly was put there in error. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. As we have some time, take all the time you need; and naturally, the Defence will have all the time it needs at its disposal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Witness. Can you hear the interpretation? Can you hear what I'm saying being interpreted into your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could you tell me your first and last name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Kruno Rajic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 1st [as interpreted] of January, 1960.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And your place of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is your address in the city you live in at the moment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now or where I lived before?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the moment, in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you live in Zagreb now. What are you by profession?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm a driver.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you're a driver. You've been called as a witness for the Prosecution to testify with regard to the events that you witnessed. Before you testify, you have to read out the solemn declaration that the usher is going to show you. Please read it out in your own language.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. You may sit down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I have said, you've been called as a witness for the Prosecution. You will be asked some questions by the representatives of the Prosecution first of all; they are to your right. Once they have concluded their examination, the Defence, who are to your left, can ask you some questions too. And if necessary, the three Judges who are before you can also ask you questions. Please try to answer the questions put to you as extensively as possible. Avoid answering by just saying yes or no. Try to elaborate when answering questions. And if there are any questions that you don't understand, ask the person who has asked you to question to put it to you again. If there are any problems of any kind at any time, do inform the Trial Chamber. Having said that, the Prosecution may now proceed with its examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President, Your Honours. Examined by Mr. Stamp:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Rajic. When did you say your date of birth is?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Good morning. The 2nd of January, 1960.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were you born?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: I was born in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In which village and municipality did you grow up?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: In Lasva, the village of Lajici --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The village of Rajici, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you do national service in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after that, did you take up some form of employment?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which was?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: I worked in a steel mill.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, up to 1992, were you working in that steel mill?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in about autumn 1992, were you mobilised into any particular organisation or unit?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: The military police, the reserve police force.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: In the BH Army. The interpreter thinks the witness said "in the BH Army."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The military police is a part of which organisation?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: The BH Army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence has something to say. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The first answer I heard was that he was a member of the reserve police force, the MUP; whereas, in the transcript, it says he was in the army. Could the witness either clarify this or could the transcript be corrected to correspond to his previous answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course. I was going to intervene, in fact, to clarify this matter. Please ask the witness the question again so that we know exactly which part of the police he belonged to. Was it the active-duty police, the reserve police, the civilian or the military police? We don't know. So it would be better to start from the beginning so that the witness can tell us what his duty was in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Rajic, you heard what was being said just now. Can you just tell us which organisation or which unit --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Oh, sorry. I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Having heard the exchange just now, Mr. Rajic, could you please just tell us which unit you were mobilised in in 1992.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: The BH Army; the reserve police force, the civilian police force.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were you based?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: In Lasva.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which police station did you report to?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Raspotocje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where is that?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: It's in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, where did you carry out your duties while you were a member of this reserve police?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: In Lasva.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, at the beginning of 1993, where were you living?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: I moved to Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you move with your family?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were living in Zenica in 1993, and you were carrying on duties as a reserve police officer in Lasva; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did anything happen in respect to you or your property in Lasva in April of 1993?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: I don't know. Do you mean when Lasva fell or before that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Lasva fall in April 1993? Fall to whom? Or what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Until the conflict broke out, no one touched anything. I was on night duty, and I -- I was at home there. But before April, until the conflict broke out between the 7th Muslim and the HVO ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, tell us what happened in April when that conflict broke out.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: About 2.000 members of the 7th Muslim Brigade came to Lasva. And then conflicts started on -- in Dusina, and then they moved from Dusina to the hill. And in the Lasva local commune, the people went to the local commune.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the 7th Muslim Brigade came to Lasva, were you there?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Later on, did you receive any information in respect to your personal property or documents?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. When I left prison. Because while I was in detention, I took my documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Very well. In April, did you receive any information in respect to your documents at Lasva? And I'm speaking about April 1993.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: No. As far as I'm concerned, nothing was touched until the conflict broke out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Let's move on. Can you recall the 22nd of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: On the 22nd, I was on the night shift in Lasva. I then went home. That was the night between the 22nd and 23rd. On the 23rd, at about 9.00 or 10.00 in the morning, the 7th Muslim arrived. They came to the flat in which I lived, Bratusa [phoen]. My child was in front of the building, and at that moment they asked him where I lived. The child said he'd take them up there. I lived on the first floor. When the child rang the bell and I opened the door, the two from the 7th Muslim, who were pointing a rifle at the child, they then told me that I should go to speak to them for about five minutes. That's how I got to the music school where -- with the 7th Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The two persons who came to your flat, why do you describe them as being members of the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Because they had a patch on their left arm. But it was the 7th Muslim Brigade, the MOS, and it said "the BH Army" just above.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe how they were dressed.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: They had camouflage uniforms and a patch on the left arm, and they had a police-style belt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They told you that you should go to speak to them for about five minutes. Did you leave with them and go anywhere?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go to?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: To the 7th Muslim Brigade in the music school, which is by the theatre, the MUP, and the Privredna Bank.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you travel to the music school?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: In a blue Renault, a sports car. It was similar to an estate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say who drove that car?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Well, a third person who was in the car, from the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why do you say that third person was from the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Because he was with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was he dressed?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Identically.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you observe anything about the car itself, any markings or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: It said "The 7th Muslim Brigade" on the door. That had been inscribed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you know this place that you called the music school before? Did you know of it before?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, as a member of the reserve police, what did you know about the Zenica music school at that time?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: I knew that when Lasva fell, a relative of mine and the neighbours who were down there, Viktor Rajic, Jozo Kristo, Srecko Kristo, Rados Perica, and Batinic - I can't remember his first name - they were in the music school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They were in the music school in -- in what capacity? What were they doing there?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: They were being held there as detainees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you arrived at the music school on the 23rd of April, what happened? You can start by telling us first where were you taken to when you arrived.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: When I got to the music school, as soon as I entered I was taken into a big room, a hall. I waited there. They told me to wait there. I waited there. While I was waiting, I phoned my brother on my mobile telephone. I asked him what I was doing there. And then this person -- one of the persons hit me and took me down to the basement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were waiting there, could you just repeat for us what you said about this telephone.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: In that room, when I got there, while I was waiting, my phone from the house, from Lasva, and my brother's one, they were there. When I said, "What's my telephone doing here," one person hit me and then took me down to the basement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went into that hall, were there other persons there?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. I saw Dragan Jonjic, my uncle, Ivo Rajic, and Franjo Strbac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Where did you see Dragan Jonjic, Ivo Rajic, and Franjo Strbac?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Down in the basement, which is where we spent 50 days. We were there all the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were there until what date? Do you recall? And when I say "there," I mean at the music school.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: From the 10th of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived there on the 23rd of April, 1993, can I take it that you remained there until the 10th of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you remain in the basement before any other persons who had taken you there spoke with you?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: I was down there all the time. I wasn't anywhere else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. When you saw Dragan and Ivo, did you observe anything about their physical condition?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Only the uncle. They beat him. But the other two, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you were put down in the basement on the 23rd of April, what next happened to you?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: On the 23rd, about 10.00 at night, a policeman came and took me up to the second floor, when Jasmin Isic came to be questioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The policeman who took you upstairs, how was he dressed?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: He was dressed in black. He had a black uniform, the one who came to fetch me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did that uniform have any markings or insignia which would indicate the unit that that person belonged to?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: No. The only thing it had was a white belt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you said he took you to the second floor. Did he take you to a room on the second floor?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went into that room, was there anyone inside the room? And if so, who?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. There was another guy in a black uniform, and there was also Jasmin Isic, whom I knew personally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was Jasmin Isic?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: He was a guard who was interrogating there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, what did you know of him before that?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: I knew that he was my wife's former teacher, and he lived in the area where my wife was from. He had a shop. I would go there. And while he was still in the Patriotic League, I used to drive him from Busovaca to his house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived in that room where you saw him that night, how was he dressed?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: He had a camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you notice any insignia or markings on that uniform?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say which unit he belonged to?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which unit was that?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: The 7th Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why do you say that?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Because I had known that from before, because his sister worked in the same bank as my wife. And when I tried to arrange things for my cousins, he would not hear of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice any writing on his uniform that night?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you arrived in the room, did he or anybody say anything to you?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: When I entered the room, I asked him, "Jasmin, why am I here?" And he said, "You Ustasha beast, I don't know you. You don't know me." And when I said that, the guy who was standing behind me hit me on the head with a baseball bat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many times did he hit you?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Every time I opened my mouth to say something, he would hit me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'd like you to just describe in your own words what happened in that room with Jasmin Isic while you were there that night.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: He interrogated me. He asked me about a guy from Lasva called Tarabica. I didn't know what to say about this person. Every time he would ask me things, I would say, "I don't know," and then the guy who was standing behind me hit me every time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did this interrogation and beating last for?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: I was up there for some ten minutes, and then as I was going back downstairs to the basement, on the staircase there were policemen standing every 2 or 3 metres, and they had truncheons in their hands. And they would they would beat me all the way down to the basement. In front of the basement, there was a grid, and there I stopped. They beat me there. Once I was well beaten over, I was allowed to go back into the basement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About how many policemen participated in this beating?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: A dozen, ten or so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what weapons or implements did they use to inflict this beating?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Shovel handles and a cable, the length of which was about 1 metre and its diameter was 50.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The diameter was 50 what?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: It was about a metre long and it was 50 -- the diameter was 50 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what condition were you in? Just describe that to us that day, when you arrived at the floor of the basement.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: I was black and blue. My nose was broken. I was bleeding. I was protecting my head. I was holding my hands on my head, protecting my head, so they were beating me on -- on the face and on the back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you eventually locked into the basement after that?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. There was an iron gate which was locked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, during your sojourn at the music school, was this the only time you were beaten?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: No. I went upstairs for interrogation five times or so, and every time I was taken for interrogation the same thing happened. And during the night, between midnight and 1.00 in the morning, a policeman would come, and they would take us out to the first floor one at a time to teach us how to sing. And as we entered that room, the light was out and there were policemen standing in two rows. And they also had shovel handles and they were beating us. We had to run this gauntlet. We had to run the gauntlet, and all the time they were beating us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just elaborate briefly on what you mean when you say they took you to teach you how to sing.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. When they said, "We're going to teach you how to sing," they meant We are going to hear you cry and -- and shout as we are beating you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you arrived at the basement in April, you said you saw three persons in the basement. Did the population of the basement remain the same, or did it change over the period of time that you were imprisoned there?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: No. The three of us were there all the time. And every three or four days other people came. And there were some 20 of us in there altogether. As many as were taken to the KP Dom, the same number would come to the music school. So our number remained the same all the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that number was approximately how many, did you say?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: About 20 of us were there at all times. The only thing is some would be taken away and then others would be brought in to replace them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you recall the names of some of the persons who were there while you were there and who were beaten? You have told us three names. If you could recall any other names, I'd like you to tell us very, very slowly so we could note them.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Last names --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Madam Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I object to this question as a question which is leading, because in the previous answers, the witness stated that only his uncle had been beaten, whereas the other two had not been beaten. And now in -- the Prosecutor in his question says that in addition to these three who were beaten, who else was beaten? I believe that the Prosecution has based this question on something that the witness did not previously say in any of his answers, so he is leading the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I am not leading the witness. But for what it is worth, to save time, if we can deal with it another way. But I'd -- perhaps it's a matter of translation, but the record of the English transcript makes it clear, in my humble view, that there is no element of leading here, according to the literal meaning of the words used; however, it would be easy to ask him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember the names of persons who were at the music school while you were there who were beaten? If you can, please tell us those names quite slowly.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Only when I arrived in the music school there were three people in addition to me, so there were four of us. My uncle had been beaten, and the other two had not been beaten. So that was on day one. That was the situation on day one. Later on we were all beaten. Everybody who came downstairs was beaten. There was this guy called Jerkovic. They cut off half of his ear. There was another guy, Slavko, I can't remember his family name. They broke his arm. And I'm going to give you other names. Badrov, Gelic, Strbac, Jerkovic, Viskovic, Vrvilo was the chief of the security station in Zenica. There was also a Serb whose name I can't remember who was also there, and his father-in-law as well, he was also there. It was very difficult to remember all of their names. They would only stay there for two or three days, and we didn't dare talk because they were listening to what we were saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Continue, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said your uncle was there? Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remind me of his name, please.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Ivo Rajic. There were some other uncles of mine there. There was another uncle of mine, but that was later on. The first uncle that I mentioned, I found him there when I first came. There was another uncle of mine that was my father's uncle and his son, who is mentally handicapped. There is also my father's uncle who was a Serb, because my father's sister was married to him. They arrived later, five days after I arrived there. My father was also there, but he was up there at the reception. He was on work obligation. He worked in the theatre across the road. They didn't take him downstairs. They, rather, let him go.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your uncle, the one who had the son who was mentally handicapped, what was his name?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Marko Rajic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the name of the son who was mentally handicapped?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Marko Rajic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the name of the uncle -- or his father, I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Franjo Rajic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the guards at the music school do anything or play any games in respect to this father and his mentally retarded son?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they tell Franjo to do anything, in respect to his son?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: One evening a policeman came with another person. He gave Franjo Rajic a club, ordering him to hit his son. He refused to do that. Then he ordered him to do it again. He ordered him to do it, and he said if he didn't do it that he would hit him. Marko's father didn't want to hit his son. And then this policeman ordered Dragan Jonjic to hit Franjo. When Dragan hit Franjo, he told him that he didn't do it properly and that he should repeat it. Dragan repeated the hit, and then the policeman again said that he didn't hit him properly. And then the policeman took the club and hit Slavko, whose family name I can't remember. I only know that his arm had already been broken and he didn't have a proper balance. He couldn't keep himself straight up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, was the -- was this the only time when something like that happened, where a guard ordered one prisoner to beat another?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About how frequent --

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that was just one time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One time what happened?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: That was just one case when they ordered any of us to hit another prisoner. But there was another policeman -- or I think he was just a foot soldier -- who was there. He came downstairs with a shovel handle. He lined us up, and he started beating us. That was during one night. And then Jusuf, whose family name I don't know and who was the commander of the police there, came downstairs and told him that he shouldn't beat us, and he kept this man downstairs for two days as a prisoner, together with the rest of us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Very well. We'll get back to you, sir. But just far clarification, was it one time or more than one time that you observed an incident where guards ordered prisoners to beat other prisoners?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: No. While we were downstairs, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No what? Could you just elaborate on your answer.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Nobody ever ordered anybody to beat us downstairs in the basement. When we were beaten, we were beaten upstairs in that big hall or when we were taken for interrogation. When we were beaten in that big hall, I suppose that their commanders were not aware of the fact that they were beating us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. What I'm asking is this: You told us of an incident where a guard asked, or told, Franjo to beat his son and also told Dragan to beat Franjo. Do you recall telling us about that? Were there other incidents of the same nature, or was that the only time a guard told a prisoner to beat or hit another prisoner?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: That was just the first time. No, that was just the first time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Residovic, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 18, line 25. To a repeat a question by my learned friend, the witness answered clearly: "It was only one time that prisoners made any of us beat another prisoner." Why is the witness forced to give a different answer when his answer was already given?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Line 25, page 18, the English translation, "Yes, that was just one time." So the answer is given, and it is "just one time." It doesn't make sense to ask the same question all over again when it is clear that this incident happened only one time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Just for the record, Mr. President - and I'm not in any case indicating that counsel is saying anything improper - but my reading of page 18, line 23 to 25 - and I think we should look at everything in context, really:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "Now, was this the only time when something like that happened, when a guard ordered one prisoner to beat another?"

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: "No."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "About how frequent?"

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: "Yes, that was just one time."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "One time what happened?"

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: "That was just one case when they ordered one of us to hit another prisoner, but there was another policeman --" And then he goes into a situation where a policeman lined them up. So what we have, at the beginning he gives one answer, "no." In the middle of a another question, he gives a different answer. And then in the third answer, he answers one way again and goes on to elaborate in a manner which clearly indicates that the witness is not following what is happening. So there is not one equivocal answer to the question. The answer to the question remains equivocal and remained equivocal until the last question that he has just answered, and that is at line 19:25 when he said that was just the first time, "No, that was just the first time." So I think on a fair and reasonable and faithful reading of the transcript - I'm not suggesting that counsel wasn't being faithful to the transcript - there were matter which is were equivocal and which ought properly to be cleared up. But in any case, on the record, it has been clarified. He has said it was not the first time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. Very well, then. Let's clarify this ambiguity. I'm going to ask the witness. The persons who guarded you, did they ask you to beat each other? Did that happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. This incident happened just once, when Franjo Rajic was ordered to ask Marko, his son. He wouldn't do it, and then Dragan was forced to beat Franjo. Dragan Jonjic hit Franjo twice, and the policeman was not satisfied. He said this was not enough. And then the second policeman who was with him took Slavko and started beating him and -- to show him how the beating was done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you're saying that this happened only once, such type of incident happened only once?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then this has been clarified. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, sorry, I thought that the answer was not recorded, but I can now see that it has been recorded. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Proceed, Mr. Stamp, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall a prisoner by the name of Pandza?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What ethnicity was he?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Croat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you recall his first name?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: No. I only know that his family name is Pandza.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall when he arrived at the music school?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: I can't remember the date, but at about 2.00 in the morning they brought him in. He was -- he had been beaten. They would beat people up in the basement. We heard children and crying. And then two persons, two policemen, took him down to the basement and left him there. Jonjic and I approached him, and Jonjic asked him what his name was. He said, "Pandza," his surname. And he then said that they would be answerable to God for having beaten him. And then those two policemen returned to the basement again, because they hadn't yet left the basement, and they continued to beat him. They had automatic rifles. They grabbed the rifles by the barrel and they started beating him with the rifles. After they had been beating him for ten minutes, they brought another two men in, and they took him away. He wasn't showing any signs of life any more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see him again after that?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: No. His mother would come after three days had passed -- or she came every third day to the music school. She was looking for her son, because people had told her that he had been taken there. But she never found out anything about him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if his mother or if anyone has seen him alive since that beating?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: No. To this very day, nothing has been found out about him. The child was a minor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was a minor?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Pandza.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And by that, you mean about how old was he?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: 16 years old.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said there were about 20 prisoners at any one time in the basement. About how big was that basement? What was the size of it?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: About 4 metres wide and 13 metres long.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you had to sleep in that place, how did you manage to sleep? What arrangements did you make to sleep or to lay down?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: There were three or four benches, about four planks. Some slept on the planks, some on the benches, and some remained sitting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were there, in particular during the first few weeks, what -- how did they feed you, if at all?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Nothing. Tea. We weren't given anything. We were only given tea, and that's when we got to the basement. We had two 50-kilo bags, nylon bags, in which there was mouldy bread. That was downstairs. We couldn't live on tea alone, so we'd try and get the mould off the bread and dunk it in the tea and eat it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For about how long did that type of meal regime - if I could call it that - last?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Until Ante Viskovic was released from prison. When he left, when he was released, Jusuf came. He had come for Ante Viskovic, who was to leave. He was in a T-shirt. Jusuf asked him, "You didn't turn up like that, did you?" He said, "No, I had a leather jacket." He said, "Where is it?" He said, "Your policeman has taken it away." Jusuf then asked, "Has anyone else had things taken?" But no one dared raise a hand. He said, "Don't worry. Nothing will happen to you." He tried to persuade us. When we raised our hands, he made a list of the items that had been taken from various individuals, and he asked us whether we knew who had done this. We then gave a rough description of the policeman in question. Jusuf called a policeman and sent him to fetch this person. When he came, we said that wasn't the right person, that it was someone else. Jusuf then sent this policeman to the line in Kacuni to fetch this person. He knew where to go, which part of the line to go to, and he sent the second one home, near Kraljeva Sutjeska, near Kakanj, to fetch some things. All of the item that is the policeman had were in -- were stored away in a freezer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So were these items recovered and returned to the prisoner who was being released?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. About what time approximately, that is, what date was Ante Viskovic released from prison and Jusuf came to the prison?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: About a month, I think, while I was down there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About a month after you'd been taken there?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were taken there, what was your weight?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 96 kilos, I take it you mean? Kilograms?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you left there, what was your weight?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again, that means 65 kilograms?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. When I left the prison.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With 20 men more or less in that basement area, what provisions were made in respect to toilet facilities?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Not in the basement. We had a bucket we could use to urinate in. But when we had to go to the toilet, that was up on the ground floor. And whenever we went up there, you'd go into the toilet, someone would kick the door, and you'd be knocked over in the toilet. And on your way back, they'd beat you again. So we tried to hold on for as long as possible not to go to the toilet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the circumstances in which Ante Viskovic was released?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: No. They didn't beat him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what arrangements were made in respect to his release?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Stjepan Siber came with us, and a relative of mine, a cousin of mine, Vladimir Barac [as interpreted], who was the president of the HVO government in Zenica. They left. They got him out.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's Correction: President of the HDZ in Zenica, not of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think the translation of what the witness said is completely unclear with regard to how Mr. Viskovic was released. So perhaps it would be good to clarify this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Mr. Stamp, it would be better to ask the witness the question again, the question about the circumstances under which Mr. Viskovic was released, since it might appear quite confusing. The witness could certainly provide clarifications.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, you heard what was said just now? Can you explain for the benefit of counsel on the other side the circumstances in which Ante Viskovic was released.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Stjepan Siber came from Sarajevo to Zenica. Vjekoslav Barac was the president of the HDZ in Zenica, and Viskovic had been the chief of security in the MUP before. And through the two of them they managed to get him out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said you moved with your family to Zenica in 1993. Did your family include a wife?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were there, did your wife --

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were locked up in the music school, did your wife make any efforts to arrange for your release?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did she speak with any person in particular in order to effect your release?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: My wife went to where the army headquarters was and locked for Dzemo Merdan there. Because when my wife went there, when she went down there, she wanted to get to the 7th Muslim Brigade. She wanted the Red Cross to come and register us. And as they didn't want to receive her, she didn't want to go away. There were long lines there. They then gave her Dzemo Merdan's telephone number, and they said she could phone about 10.00 in the evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did she speak with Dzemo Merdan in order to try to get you released?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, she did. She spoke to him and said they should go to the 7th Muslim Brigade in the music school, and she was told the 7th Muslim Brigade isn't there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who -- go on.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: When Dzemo asked her why I had been imprisoned, my wife said because he's a Croat -- or rather, because his name is Kruno. He said, "There are other Krunos in Zenica." And my wife answered, "Haven't you managed to capture all of them?"

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Very well. Just listen to what I'm asking you. I know that the President told you that you could elaborate, but if you could just for this -- this set of questions be as brief as you can. Who was Dzemo Merdan?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: He was an officer for negotiations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: An officer of what organisation or group?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Of the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did your wife want to speak with him?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Because he was from Merdan. And when the Lasva HVO fell, we were on duty at the time. UNPROFOR and Dzemo Merdan were in my house and persuaded me -- tried to persuade me to return to Lasva, so we knew him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, apart from knowing him, do you know if he had had any reason to do anything, in respect to any prisoner, at the Zenica Music School?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: I haven't understood the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recall somebody by the name of Ivan Borotinski?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Ivan Borotinski, yes. He was captured in Busovaca and taken to the KP Dom in Zenica. Dzemo Merdan got him out of prison and left him in his aunt's flat in Zenica. Jasmin Isic found out that he was in the aunt's flat and took him to the Music School, to the basement where we were.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have now heard a very detailed answer, but we don't know how the witness came to know these facts because the Prosecution hasn't informed us of the basis of his knowledge. So we are talking about hearsay information.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, isn't that a matter for cross-examination, if counsel thinks -- is this an objection? I don't understand why I'm being interrupted. Am I going to be told -- could it be explained to me what is happening here. I'm not sure I understand what is happening here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I think that the problem is that if we have a look at lines 12 to 15 we've moved from a situation that relates to Merdan and someone called Ivan Borotinski. The Trial Chamber has just found out about the existence of these individuals. Within the framework of the examination-in-chief, the witness said of his own accord that this person had been captured, taken to the Zenica prison, and that Merdan got him released. So obviously it would have been necessary to ask him how he knew about this. Did he witness this event? Did he see Borotinski in the prison at the same time that he was there? So we don't know. It's quite confusing. But you'll have time to think about this matter before continuing with the examination-in-chief. It is now half past 10.00, and we have to have our so-called technical break. So we will break for 25 minutes and resume at five to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We resume, and I give the floor to the Prosecution, who are probably going to try and clarify the situation that arose on the last page of the transcript, starting with line 2 onwards. We would like the know whether the events that the Defence [as interpreted] have mentioned are the events that he himself participated in or does this -- his knowledge arise from hearsay. Did he participate in these events personally, or were they described to him? So this is what the Trial Chamber would like to know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I heard all that from Ivan Borotinski. So this is the knowledge that I received from him. And he was a participator in the event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the witness has told us that he learned about the events from Ivan Borotinski. The Prosecution, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, back to where we were. You said something about Jasmin Isic. Did Borotinski, was he taken to the Zenica Music School?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. From his aunt's apartment, he was transferred to the musical school. He was also a minor at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, while he was there -- or while you were at the music school, was Borotinski released from the music school?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how arrangements were made for him to be released?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: I don't know how he was released. I only know that his aunt came to Jasmin to ask him about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did his aunt come alone?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: I don't know. We were downstairs. The iron gate was open, and we heard her looking for Jasmin Isic. The policeman asked her who she was, and then she said she was young Ivan's aunt. We heard all that while we were in the basement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Do you know whether or not Dzemo Merdan did anything in this regard?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When Ivan's aunt went to the Zenica Music School, do you know if she spoke with him, Ivan?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. Ivan went upstairs to the landing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did he return to the basement?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he tell you who he spoke with?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did he say he spoke with?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: With his aunt, who also brought us some food, for the rest of us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how long after that he was released?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Three days later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you told who arranged this?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: No. He went to be exchanged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you told -- I asked earlier if you were told who arranged the release. Were you told who arranged the exchange?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness has already answered this question. I don't see a reason to insist on the questions to which the witness clearly cannot give a more precise answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to say to the Defence that within their cross-examination they can address that. And on the examination-in-chief, the Prosecution can ask all the questions that prove the fact that they want to establish and during the cross-examination, the Defence will have the opportunity to ask any questions to contest the establishment of the facts by the witness if they deem that they should be contested. Also, if the witness has answered very precisely to a question, it is not necessary to re-ask the question again, because that's how we waste time. The question of the efficiency of the proceedings is at stake, so we are not going to ask the same question if we have had a precise answer. If the answer was not precise, then we have the right to re-ask the question again. Having said that, let's proceed. Mr. Stamp, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said earlier that someone -- while your wife was making efforts on your behalf, someone told her that the 7th Muslim Brigade were not at the music school. Who -- how did you learn this?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Can you please elaborate. Can you explain what you mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your wife -- according to you, your wife had been making efforts to effect your release from the music school. And in the course of doing so, she was told that the 7th Muslim Brigade was not at the music school.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. Dzemo Merdan claimed that there was no prison at the music school. He said that to my wife.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Subsequent to that, did Dzemo Merdan do anything in respect to your wife's request that something be done about your imprisonment there?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if Dzemo Merdan ever went to the music school?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. You said conditions improved when Jusuf came to the music school. Jusuf was a guard there.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was he there?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: I think he was the commander of the military police in the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the Red Cross visit you while you were at the music school?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About when was the first time that they visited while you were there?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: I don't know the date. They tried once to visit us. Strbac, Jonjic and I were taken to the first floor, to a room up there, and the rest of the detainees, some 17 of them, were taken to a van and transported to Bilmiste, to a school there. And that's where they stayed one whole day. And in the evening, after nobody had appeared, they returned those detainees to the basement. I think that on the 16th of May the Red Cross were successful at their second attempt. Again, identical steps were taken. The three of us were taken upstairs to the same room, and the rest were again transported by a van to Bilmiste.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were there, do you know if the other persons, those who were transported away to Bilmiste, were ever visited by Red Cross personnel?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were eventually transferred to the KP Dom; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was this?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: On the 10th of June. I stayed in the KP Dom until the 19th of June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And thereafter, you were released from the KP Dom; is that correct? On the 19th of June, were you released from the KP Dom or were you transferred to somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: On the 19th, I was exchanged in Zenica. On my way from the Music School, Jasmin told me that I should not go anywhere, that I should stay in Zenica. Jasmin Isic knew that I had my two sisters-in-law in Germany. Two of my wife's sisters were living in Germany, and he knew that. And he asked me to pay him, to give him money to be released. I told him I didn't have any money. And then he told me that if I went to Busovaca he would detain my wife and my children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Rajic, when you were released from the KP Dom or exchanged, as you put it, were you given any document in respect to your release?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us about that document. What document was it? And from whom did you get it?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: It was from the BH Army, and it was a paper indicating when I was brought to the Music School and when I was released from the Music School. When I was being released, they gave me a paper indicating that my original documents had been retained by the 7th Muslim Brigade. And I still have that paper.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would you be able to recognise and identify a copy of that paper if you saw it again?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: With your leave, Mr. President, Your Honours, I propose to show to the witness a document and ask if he can tell us what it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do we have a hard copy of this document for the Bench?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes. I propose to --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now we can see the document on the screen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the left of the screen is the document that I want to show the witness. On the right is a translation of the document into English. Yes. What is that document you have in front of you, sir, or which is on the left-hand side of the screen?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: This is my discharge letter from the prison. And the date showing on the discharge letter are the dates of my imprisonment and of my release. And it says also that all my documents, the ID card, the driving licence, have been retained at the Music School.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's a part of the document written in hand immediately above the stamp. Who wrote that?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: They did [Realtime transcript read in error "I did"].

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you put the document on the ELMO, Madam Usher, please. On the ELMO. The B/C/S. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have a look there to the document to your right, sir, to your right. Not the screen. To your right. Do you see the stamp near to the bottom of the document?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see writing in hand immediately above the stamp?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you point to it, please.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: For the record, the witness points to handwriting above the words -- above the typewritten words "Zenica, 17.6.1993." And it's now highlighted on the -- highlight both lines please -- on the Sanction technology.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who wrote that?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: This is what I received as I was being released from the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I asked you who wrote that earlier, and you told me "I did." I just want to clarify. Who wrote that handwritten part that you just pointed to. Point to it again, please.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: They did. They did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oh, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much. It could be removed now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you said "persons" -- withdrawn. Let's start again. While you were at the Music School, you said persons were regularly taken upstairs and beaten. When they returned to the basement, in what condition did you see or observe were they?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Every person who came downstairs first would go upstairs to that room. They would be interrogated and beaten there. And then they would return to the basement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what I want to know is when they returned to the basement after being beaten, what did you observe about their physical condition?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: They were in poor shape.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And by "poor shape," what did you see?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Let me give you Jerkovic as an example. Half of his ear was hanging. Slavko's arm was broken. Slavko couldn't control his movements. As soon as he would stand up, he would fall down like a burnt candle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these things you could observe of them?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said prisoners who had been beaten at the Music School were from time to time transferred to the KP Dom. Were they transferred in this condition from time to time?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you explain to us what you mean by that.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Firstly, those who were supposed to be transferred, they would be allowed to recover. They would not beat them prior to transfer. And then they would transfer them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, you said earlier that the commanders probably did not know of the beatings that took place. On what basis do you express that opinion?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Because Jusuf only learnt when Viskovic was being released. Viskovic told him that we had been beaten, and then Jusuf said, "While I'm here in command, no harm should befall you. When you are taken to be interrogated, nothing should happen to you while I'm here."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, was anyone beaten after Jusuf came there?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: No, not after that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many times did you see Jasmin Isic at the Music School?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Five times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And apart from the first time you saw him, did you observe any writing on his attire when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said earlier that one prisoner had been asked -- withdrawn.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That's the examination-in-chief, may it please you, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before giving the floor to the Defence, I would like to ask the Prosecution whether the document that you have presented from the military in Zenica, do you want to tender this document into evidence? I'm asking the Prosecution whether this document, do you want to tender this document from the military district in Zenica into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed, Mr. President. Now or at the end of testimony, whatever pleases the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's up to you to make that choice.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: We tender it and ask that it be received in evidence. But the thing is when. Sometimes some Chambers prefer to do it at the end of testimony; sometimes some Chambers will do it in the middle of testimony. I will do it in any way that the Court finds it pleasing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We are going to hear the cross-examination. Just a brief remark: I have a copy which is in B/C/S, but it is not legible. There are some black stains. You're saying that there is also an original. I wonder whether the original is in the same state. If it isn't, then can I have a better copy. If your original is in better shape, then the Trial Chamber should not receive a copy which is hardly legible.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The gentleman has just told us that he has an original in his hands. I'm showing you the copy that I've been given. There are black stains, making the copy illegible.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the future, please, if you want to tender a document into evidence, make sure that the copy that we receive is in as good a condition as possible so that there are no technical problems with reading the document that we are being given. The problem, I believe, arises from the copy that we have, rather than from the original that the gentleman has in his possession. Having said this, before we give the floor to the Defence, I have two questions for the witness. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, within the examination-in-chief, you have spoken about Jasmin Isic and about a person called Merdan. So you have mentioned two persons that you know. According to your knowledge, are these two persons still alive? Do they still reside in the area? Or are they maybe missing? What do you know about these two people? Have you ever seen them or have you ever heard being spoken of them since that time, since May 1993? What can you tell us about that?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Jasmin Isic worked in an elementary school in Gavrine Kuce. That's all I know about him. I personally saw him there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question I'm asking: These two persons at this moment in January 2004, are they still in the region or are they missing from the region?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I reside in Zagreb. I'm living in Zagreb, so I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You don't know. Very well. And the second question that I want to put to you concerns Mr. Jusuf. You have mentioned Mr. Jusuf's name on several occasions. In your opinion, was he a member of the military or was he a civilian?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: He was a soldier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was a soldier. Was he a local Muslim or was he a foreign Muslim?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: He was local.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was a local Muslim. And was Mr. Jusuf performing his duties when you were imprisoned, or did you only find out about him afterwards? On the first day you spent in that school was he already there or was it only at a later date that you found out about him?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: He was there all the time, but we didn't know who he was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And that means that when you were taken to the school, on the day that you were arrested by two policemen - and there was a third one who was driving the vehicle - according to what you are saying, he was there, he should have been there, as someone who had duties to perform there.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I can see that Mr. Stamp is standing. Is there anything that Mr. Stamp would like to add, perhaps with regard to the document before the Defence takes the floor? Very briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: My apology in respect to the difficulty in reading the document, the poor legibility thereof. We do try to tender to the Court the best copies of what we have in our evidence unit, but the witness has brought a copy. What I propose to do -- or brought what I can see and know is the original -- is to ask him if he's prepared to part with it. Or if not, if the registrar could be asked to take possession of it just for the purpose of trying to get the best possible copy, a new photocopy of that document. So may I just first ask: Is that the original of the document which I showed you earlier? Is it? Please answer. Is it the original?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Madam Usher, could you show the original to the Defence so that everyone can see it. Show it to both the accused, show it to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And we will have a look at the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the basis of the original - and both parties have examined it - we have come to the conclusion that the document is the same. The difference between the copy and the original consists in fact that what has been handwritten is in blue, whereas the copy is in black. So the handwritten part is in blue in the original. The colour of the signature is the same. We can see that there is a stamp on the document. It appears to be an official stamp. And there is a mark in the centre, a coat of arms with three lilies in the upper-right part and two or three lilies to the left, and there is a white stripe in the centre of this coat of arms and there is something written in B/C/S. I can't translate it, as I don't know B/C/S. The copy we have been provided with resembles the document we have mentioned. It's not necessary to make any copies. But the difference between the document that the witness has and the photocopy is that the photocopy contains his name and initials, and there is a date "30/7" and there is a "0." Witness, on the copy, did you subsequently write down your name and initials? Madam Usher, could you show the witness his document and the copy with his name and the date, and he'll explain to us why there is a difference between the two documents. So, Witness, with regard to the documents that you have and the photocopy, your name and initials are on the photocopy; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. Because I handed over this document, I don't know. When I was asking to go into a third country, to another country, on that occasion I put my signature on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So you had to -- you must have signed on the 30th of July, 2001 or 2002, because we can't read the date. You don't know the year?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes -- no. Because I have copies at home.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So you can't. If the document is not contested, this copy -- the copy of the document will be tendered into evidence, but we will await for the conclusion of the cross-examination to do so. Could you give me the copy, and you will keep your own document. Having carried out this expert work, the Defence may now take the floor to proceed with their cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Cross-examined by Ms. Residovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And good day, Mr. Rajic. My name is Edina Residovic, and I am Defence counsel for General Hadzihasanovic. I'd be grateful if you could answer some questions that I'm going to put to you, and I will also ask you to wait for the end of the translation of my question and then answer. That will enable everyone to follow what we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, in addition to the questions that fall within the scope of the examination-in-chief and in accordance with Rule 90(H)(ii), I'm going to ask the witness to answer several general questions about the situation in Zenica, because Mr. Rajic -- an examination of that situation is of general interest for my client. Mr. President, you will allow me to ask some questions of this general nature. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, you said that in 1992 you were living with your family in the local commune of Lasva, in the Rajici hamlet; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The local commune -- or, rather, the village of Lasva is at the estuary -- is at the confluence of the Lasva River and the Bosna River, which is at the crossroads towards Sarajevo, Zenica, and Travnik. Or as we say, it was at the so-called Lasva junction. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That junction is of great strategic importance, especially for the connection of Zenica to Sarajevo, Visoko, and Kiseljak; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because of the fact that the Serbian forces had occupied part of the main road which goes through the valley of the River Bosna towards Sarajevo, the road through the Lasva junction was the only connection of Zenica with other territory which was under the control of the BH Army and with the main routes of supply in Bosnia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be correct to say that the other supply route in this territory in which you lived and which you are familiar with went through Prozor, passed through Prozor, and Gornji Vakuf, but at the end of 1992 and the beginning of 1993 the conflict between the BH Army and the HVO made it impossible to supply Central Bosnia via that route?
