Are you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Well, not really.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Naturally, Mr. Rajic, you will only tell me what you are aware of, so I thank you for that answer. The local commune of Lasva, like most of Bosnia and Herzegovina, was a place of mixed ethnic composition, and the relations between all the ethnic groups were very good; is that correct? And I'm referring to the pre-war period.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Before the war, yes, that was so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You worked in a big factory in the Zenica ironworks, and the relations between all the ethnic groups before the war were very good; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be correct to say that soon after the elections held in 1990, which were won by nationalist parties, you did not want to join any f the nationalist parties?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But your cousin, Zvonko Rajic, at the beginning of the attack, directed at Bosnia and Herzegovina founded an HVO unit in Lasva; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. But there were Croats and Muslims who were together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Lasva belonged to the municipality of Zenica.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This HVO unit didn't have any links with the Jure Francetic Brigade in Zenica. It was connected to the HVO Brigade in Busovaca. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be correct to say that in the autumn of 1992 Zenica had been blocked by the Serbian forces and that the town was even bombed from the air? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The wartime situation was the reason for which you, who worked in the Zenica ironworks, were mobilised into the MUP reserve police force in Zenica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Zenica MUP is a civilian police force; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The civilian police and the BH Army were two parts of the BH armed forces; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, the police had a separate line of command, so you were subordinated to the BH MUP; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the beginning, you performed the duties of a reserve policeman, but at the same time you worked in a factory; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us when you started performing the duties of a reserve policeman on a full-time basis.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: When the Serbs died in Lasva, on Christmas -- Bozici. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So from the autumn 1992, you were engaged as a reserve policeman of the Zenica MUP at all time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At some time towards the end of 1992 and at the beginning of 1993, the relations between the HVO and the BH Army deteriorated; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The HVO unit in Lasva would gather in front of the cafe that belonged to Zvonko Rajic's brother, and on some occasions these gatherings were rowdy. And on one occasion, they fired from firearms, and your son managed to avoid being hit by that bullet. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The checkpoint held by the HVO in Lasva, which was not far away from the station, the railway station, was in fact on the road between the Lasva junction and the pass to the Dusina village.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: No. That was at the railway station, that pass towards that headed in the direction of Dolipolje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The reasons you have mentioned now, the increased tension with the HVO, the insecurity in Lasva itself, this is something I want to ask you about. You should tell me: This wartime situation, the lack of security, were these the reasons for which at the beginning of January 1993 you decided to move to Zenica with your family?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As of that time, you performed your duties as a reserve policeman in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: I spent some time in Zenica and some time in Crkvice. There was -- the 5th Police Station was in Crkvice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time of the armed conflict that broke out in Lasva -- or rather, in Dusina on the 26th of January, you weren't in the area. At that time, you were performing your duties in Zenica. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: No. The night before that happened, I was on duty in Lasva.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But on the day of the event itself, you weren't in Lasva.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: No, no, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After these events in Dusina sometime at the beginning of February, the Zenica MUP brought its contingent in Lasva up to strength in order to protect people and property; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That contingent included 15 reserve policemen and you and your cousin, Vlado Rajic, were also part of the contingent; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The boundaries of your local commune, Lasva, the village of Dusina and Brdo, are in fact on the front lines between the army and the HVO; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, I'm now going to ask you about what you know about the work of the Zenica MUP itself. When working in the MUP, you know and you saw that there were a lot of people who were in the MUP who worked for the police before the war too; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the war, the Zenica MUP had good technical equipment and good professionals; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the same time, at the beginning of 1993 they started forming BH Army brigades in Zenica, and the 3rd Army Corps was established; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, those units and the military police were joined by mobilised people on the whole who didn't have much experience, as far as police duties were concerned; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was the reason for which, quite frequently and at the request of the BH Army, the MUP helped carrying out on-site investigations, they helped carry out controls and provide expert reports, et cetera; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Quite frequently, at the request of the BH Army, joint patrols were conducted and they performed certain duties together; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, are you aware of the fact that before the 3rd Corps was established, from the very beginning of the war they started forming various military units in Zenica. For example, the Patriotic League, the Green Berets, the Muslim forces, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be correct to say that after the brigades had been formed and after they had been formally subordinated to those units, a large number of those units remained under the direct influence of the religious and political leaders who had founded them?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: All I know is that the 7th Muslim Brigade was the main one in Zenica, whereas the 3rd Corps had no importance whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be correct to say that some other centres had a lot of influence over various military formations in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: The 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the same time as the corps and brigades were formed, you know that the army was involved in a conflict on a large front with the Serbian forces which weren't far from Zenica; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the beginning of 1993, as you have already said, a conflict broke out with the HVO too, first of all in Busovaca and Kiseljak, and later on in other areas too; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: First this occurred in Lasva and Krcine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, in any event, throughout that period of time, in the spring of 1993, there were armed conflicts between these two formations in various places; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the town of Zenica, there were also HOS and HVO units who were operational, and their lines of command were quite separate from the BH Army; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, is it correct to say that as of 1992 the situation in Zenica became more complicated because of the large number of refugees arriving in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first wave of refugees arrived from Krajina and from Eastern Bosnia and they'd been driven out by the Serbian forces; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the days following the fall of Jajce, several thousand refugees could enter Zenica in one day; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Such a situation created enormous problems, as far as providing food and accommodation for the population is concerned.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the beginning of the conflict between the army and the HVO, refugees from areas under the control of the HVO in Busovaca, Kiseljak, and Vitez started arriving in Zenica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. After these general questions, I'm going to go back to the part that you testified about on the examination-in-chief concerning the difficult moments you had in Zenica. On the 23rd of April, as you said, from your apartment you were taken to the Music School; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Immediately prior to that, a few days before that, on the 19th of April, there was an armed conflict between the BH Army and Jure Francetic Brigade of the HVO in Zenica itself; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: There were no conflicts. Zivko Tocic was stopped in Brist by armed Mujahedins and by foreign Mujahedins. They intercepted them. They killed his nephew. He was his bodyguard. And they took Zivko out to Arnauti.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you in Zenica then?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was on the 16th of April.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: I was there when he was taken away, when this all happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, is it true that a few days after that a number of members of the Jure Francetic Brigade surrendered, whereas the rest of them left to the area under the control of the HVO via Ovnak? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Both these things happened a few days before your incarceration; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During those days, after the surrender of the Jure Francetic Brigade, a number of HVO and Croats from Zenica were brought to Zenica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were taken to the Music School, as you have already said, and they wanted to take your statement; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isic, who interrogated you, he asked you about who helped Ivica Kristo, a member of the HVO, to escape, who gave you the apartment in Zenica, and he wanted you to surrender the radio that you had in your possession; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is. However, I didn't have that radio set. It was not in my possession.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I said allegedly you had it, and you said that when you answered that you didn't have it and that you didn't know anything about it they beat you up. I'm just reiterating your -- what you said in your examination-in-chief. Although you are already spoken about that, I would still like to ask you once again: Is it correct that most of the persons who were brought into the Music School stayed there only for a brief period of time, two or three days, and then they would be either released or transferred to the KP Dom? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, they would be brought in, and then they would be transferred to the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Some people, like your father, and some other people stayed only a couple of hours and then they were released; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: People from Lasva were transferred from the Music School to the KP Dom, and them released after an hour or so. Those were people from Lasva.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, only you, Jonjic and Strbac remained incarcerated in the basement of the Music School throughout that period.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were others as well, but we were there throughout this whole period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have just mentioned that some of your relatives were incarcerated in the Music School.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that after the conflict which broke out on the 26th of January in Dusina and Lasva, your relatives were brought in at that time. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it also correct that they were exchanged at the beginning of February and went to Busovaca from the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You saw them when you arrived in Busovaca in January --

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: No, I was never in Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you left Zenica.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: No. When I left the prison, I returned to the police. I was there for six months. And then I paid 1200 marks to be able to move to Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise. Maybe we are talking at cross-purposes. I am talking about your release in January 1994. When you left Zenica, was that the first time when you saw your relatives who had been exchanged at the beginning of February and left for Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this was the first time. And you heard from then what had happened to them in the Music School; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Jusuf, who according to you was the commander of the music school -- police in the Music School, visited you some -- a month or so after you were first imprisoned.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: He was there all the time, but we didn't know who he was. We didn't know who he was until the moment this other guy was released and complained that he had been beaten, and then he told us that he was in charge of us. We would see him up there, because us prisoners would be cleaning the toilets and we would be sweeping the floor and the corridors. We would see him, but we didn't know who he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So neither you nor any other prisoners knew that he was the commander, and you never told him that you had been beaten by some of the guards before Viskovic was being released.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To the Prosecutor's question, you answered that when he saw one of the prison guards entering the basement to beat you, he disciplined that guard and put him into prison for two days; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So after having listened to all of you, he investigated into the case of your lost property. He managed to locate the whereabouts of your property, and he returned your belongings to you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that he also found the person who had taken your belongings from you and from then on you never saw this guard in the Music School? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that some guards enabled you to receive food and clothes from your families?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, there was one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He enabled this to you and to other prisoners.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, he helped us to receive food in the Music School from our families.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You even sometimes had an opportunity to meet members of your family. You met with your wife.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was the only one who was enabled such an encounter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To the Prosecutor's question, you have explained that the International Red Cross came to the Music School. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that on one occasion even representatives of the international organisation in white uniforms visited the Music School? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On both these occasions, together with two other prisoners, you spoke with these representatives; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On both these occasions, the other prisoners had been transferred from the Music School, and they were returned only when it was certain that the visitors had left; is that true?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On these two occasions, you never told the representatives of these two international organisations about the bad treatment that you received in the Music School.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: There was a microphone in the room where we were, so we were listened to on both these occasions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you either knew or you suspected that there were microphones. You therefore didn't tell the representatives of these two international organisations the truth about the treatment that you received there.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Basically you told them that you were treated well.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's exactly what I told them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you tell them, actually? That you were not beaten?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. They asked us whether we were beaten. I said sometimes. And we did not mention anything about the treatment that we received downstairs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your answers so far. Let me just consult my papers and see how far I've got with my questions. On the 10th of June, 1993, according to your testimony, you were transferred to the KP Dom in Zenica; is that true?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the treatment there was good.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You received food on a regular basis.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: We received food three times a day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your family could visit you.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They could leave some food and clothes with you.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were released from the KP Dom after 90 days; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: After 60 days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: After nine days. I was admitted on the 10th, and I was released on the 19th, so I stayed there for nine days.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the usher assist me, please, and show the witness the document that the Prosecution showed him a little while ago. The document is held by the registrar. I can give him my copy. This is the letter of discharge. Can you please put it on the ELMO, Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, this is the document that you testified about a little while ago. Both the Prosecution and the President of the Chamber had questions to ask you about this document, so I'm not going to ask you anything about this document. All I want to hear from you is to read what it says on the stamp which is on this discharge letter, the inscription on the stamp. Let me assist you. It says "The Republic of Bosnia Herzegovina" in the Latin script and in the Cyrillic script. And underneath "The District Military Court," again, in both scripts. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct. I can see it much better on my original.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were given this paper by a judge of the district military court; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we do not have any objections to admitting this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A little while ago you said that after being released from the KP Dom you continued working in the Zenica MUP. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your immediate superior in the Zenica MUP was Jasmin Jaganjac; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You received all your back salaries covering the time while you were absent from work; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You never told anybody in the MUP officially what had happened to you in the Music School; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did not report either to your MUP or the military police. You didn't file any criminal charges against the persons who had ill-treated you in the Music School; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Throughout all this time while you worked in the Zenica MUP, you didn't hear of anybody else filing criminal charges against the people who had ill-treated them in the Music School.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: That's correct. But I want -- I asked for my belongings to be returned. They had taken my car, my tractor, and they never gave me any receipt. And they -- when I asked for all these things, they chased me out of the rooms of the Territorial Defence. I was supposed to receive a receipt for my belongings, but they never wanted to give it to me. In the Territorial Defence; not in the Music School.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In January 1994, according to your own wish and paying certain persons a certain amount of money, you managed to leave Zenica and go to Kiseljak; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was then that for the first time you gave a statement to the HVO about what had happened to you in the Music School; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: I was first imprisoned by them for two days, and then in the prison I gave this statement about my prior whereabouts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this was the first time that you gave an official statement to any organ about what had happened to you in the Music School; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that, you joined the HVO.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Rajic. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The Defence of Mr. Kubura, do you have any questions to ask?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. We do have a few questions for Mr. Rajic. Cross-examined by Mr. Ibrisimovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Rajic, on behalf of Mr. Kubura, I'm going to ask you a few questions within the scope of what you have already told before this Trial Chamber today. You have already confirmed that you were a member of the reserve police of the MUP; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have also confirmed that the Ministry of the Interior also was part of the then-armed forces of the then-Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a member of the MUP, you also were a member of the armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 22nd of April, 1993, members of the 7th Muslim Brigade arrived and entered your apartment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: First they came to my house in Lasva and then they came to my apartment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You recognised these soldiers because they had patches on their left shoulder; is that correct? Is that true?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These soldiers did not have any insignia on their shoulders showing this they were members of the military police.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: No, they didn't have any such patches. They had patches. They had patches on the shoulder, not on ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived in the Music School, you found Dragan Jonjic and Franjo Strbac there. They were members of the HVO. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All the persons that you found in the Music School who -- and who arrived later were men; is that true?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There were no women in the Music School.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: No, there weren't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The person who interrogated you was Jasmin Isic, whom you knew from before; is that true?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He -- you said that he interrogated you five times and that he asked you questions that he wanted to know answers to.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These interrogations were always at night; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the moment when you were being interrogated, that is, during the night, the commander was not there; he was not in the Music School. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was interested in the escape of Ivica Kristo, a member of the HVO; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ivica Kristo was being looked for because of the money and because of the property he had; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Jasmin Isic personally asked you to give him 50.000 German marks to release you.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: I didn't give him that, because my wife found two persons that I could be exchanged for, but he wouldn't let me be exchanged. My uncle, who had been released, resided in my apartment and then he was exchanged. Through him my wife found two persons for whom I could have been exchanged. Those persons were from the 17th Krajina Brigade from Travnik. Jasmin Isic would not, however, let me be exchanged for those two persons without the money.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your sojourn within the Music School, you had contacts with other -- during your sojourn in the Music School, you had contacts with other persons who were incarcerated there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, with all the other detainees. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And other persons confirmed to you that Jasmin Isic was interested in their assets; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One of those persons is Ivan Borotinski; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The reason for which Ivan Borotinski was able to leave the Music School was that somebody paid for his release; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: I suppose so, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have confirmed earlier today that your personal belongings were returned to you when the commander of the military police intervened.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: I personally went to the Music School to fetch them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not referring to the period when you were released from the KP Dom. I'm referring to the period when Commander Jusuf asked you about your personal belongings.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, these belongings were returned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The belongings were also returned to other prisoners.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, to all of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm that one of those person's names is Jusuf Karalic?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that these belongings were held by a member of the 7th Muslim Brigade who resided in Kakanj or near Kakanj.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Kraljeva Sutjeska near Kakanj is some 40 kilometres from the Music School.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you one more question, sir: Are you aware of the fact that Jasmin Isic is being tried before the cantonal court and that you are one of the aggrieved persons in those proceedings?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: I know that he was brought in before that court, but I didn't know any other details.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have no further questions of this witness. Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to thank the Defence. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, a little while ago I asked you whether you knew the whereabouts of Jasmin Isic, and you said that you didn't know. The Defence have just told you that there are proceedings that the cantonal court against him. And now you've just replied that you were aware that -- aware of these proceedings. Why didn't you reply honestly a little while ago that you knew the whereabouts of Jasmin Isic?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: I only know that the person from the 7th Muslim Brigade who helped me, that Jasmin Isic was at one point brought in. But I do know not the current whereabouts of Jasmin Isic. I don't know where he is at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. Let's regulate the issue of the document. Can you put your name on the document that you have in front of you and also can you put today's date on this document so that this document may be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please show the document to the Prosecution, to the Defence and the accused. Mr. Registrar, please give me a number for the document in B/C/S and the translation in English.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the B/C/S version will be -- will have the exhibit number P41, and the English translation will have the exhibit number P41/E.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Any re-examination from the Prosecution? We have a few minutes before the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Briefly. Re-examined by Mr. Stamp:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who is Jusuf Karalic?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: The commander who was in the 7th Brigade in the military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is he the same commander who, so to speak, rescued your personal belongings? Is that the same person you referred to earlier as Jusuf, who managed to retrieve your belongings that had been taken by some guard?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was the first time you saw him? Now, listen to me carefully, listen to the question: When was the first time you used your eyes and saw him at the Music School?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Maybe the fifth time when I went upstairs to clean, but I didn't know who he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said you had been taken up for interrogation and beaten about five times.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first time you saw him, was that after all the times that you had been beaten during interrogation?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: I used to see him in the room where we were beaten during the night. That's where I would see him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You said the first time you saw him was about the fifth time that you went upstairs to clean. Now, can you just approximate for us about how long was that after you had been brought to the Music School.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Approximately on the seventh day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said approximately a month after you were brought there conditions were improved when Jusuf -- withdrawn. Let me rephrase. I think you said that approximately one month after being brought to the Music School Viskovic was released and Jusuf intervened and thereafter the conditions improved. Did you say that and is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Yes, Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, my colleague has already asked this question in the course of the examination-in-chief, and these questions weren't matters that were raised when the witness was cross-examined.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The Trial Chamber notes that these questions have already been put to the witness, and in the course of the cross-examination his response didn't quite tally, so either he can no longer remember, as these events happened ten years ago and his memory might be faulty, and we can fully understand that. It's true that today we don't know whether he saw Jusuf seven days after he arrived there or one month after his detention period commenced. Witness, on the basis of the questions put to you by the Prosecution and Defence, I think you have understood that what we want to know is when exactly you found out or -- that Mr. Jusuf was there or saw Mr. Jusuf. If you don't know, just say that you can't remember. And if you are sure of when this happened, tell us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I saw Jusuf immediately when I arrived, but I didn't know who this person was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So we have a new piece of information. You saw Jusuf as soon as you arrived at the school, but you didn't know who he was.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So when exactly did you find out who he was? When did you realise that he was the commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the time that Viskovic left, because at that point in time he introduced himself. It's difficult to know at the time what their names were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you're telling us that you found out about this, you found out that he was the commander for sure when Viskovic was released; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Are there any other questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Just if I could be given ten seconds to try to digest what has been said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's true that we're moving fast.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I just want to make one thing absolutely clear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Jusuf, you saw Jusuf as soon as you arrived at the school. Can I take it from that answer that Jusuf was at the school from time to time from the 23rd of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: He was there all the time, but we didn't know his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Yes, I can see that Defence counsel is getting up.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, having allowed the Prosecution to re-examine, would you allow me to just ask the witness one question which might help us clarify this matter?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Go ahead. To the extent that the question might clarify the matter, you are allowed to ask such questions. Further cross-examination by Mr. Ibrisimovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Rajic, you have confirmed that your interrogation by Mr. Isic always took place at night. You said that that happened on five occasions.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While Mr. Isic was interrogating you at night, could you confirm that Mr. Jusuf Karalic, the commander of the military police at the time, was not present in the Music School?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, given that you have allowed us to ask questions that would clarify matters, I have one question that I would like to put to the witness. Further cross-examination by Ms. Residovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is something that is not clear, but I think you could help us understand this. You said that when on the fifth time you went to clean the room, you saw Mr. Jusuf Karalic on that occasion; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that, you said that that was the same room that you were taken to at night and it was room in which you were beaten.

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But when you saw Mr. Karalic it was daytime and on that occasion you weren't tortured or interrogated; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. We would see him during the day, not at night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the room was the same room, but the circumstances were different; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Yes, the last question to clarify matters. Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If it pleases you, Mr. President, there were probably quite a few questions in -- in what I see described here as further cross-examination. I submit that I'm entitled to re-examination in respect to all of those questions. I think they did go a little bit overboard, but -- I didn't interrupt them, but I think I'm entitled to re-examine to any cross-examination that they have engaged in. I will be brief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Go ahead. Go ahead. Further re-examination by Mr. Stamp:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This Jusuf that was there from the 23rd of April, was he in a position to observe the injuries on the prisoners, including yourself, that resulted from the beatings that all of you were receiving from the 23rd of April and even before? A simple question: Was Jusuf in a position to observe, as you observed, the physical results on your bodies from the beatings that you and all the -- and the other prisoners received from the 23rd of April and even before?

utterances.speaker: KRUNO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, your examination and cross-examination have been concluded. We thank you for having come to The Hague to testify. We wish you a good trip home. And the usher will now escort you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before we adjourn, following the examination of this witness and the revelation by the Defence of Jasmin Isic, in order for the Trial Chamber to be fully informed, there are several possibilities: Either Prosecution will have this person come as a witness; or the Defence will reserve the right of calling this person as a witness. If neither party takes advantage of this possibility, the Trial Chamber will deliberate. On the basis of Rule 98, we can call this witness to the extent that this witness was present at the site in question. And we have been informed by the Defence that proceedings have been instituted against this person in Zenica. So this witness is a real witness; he exists. And we could call the witness to testify here in good time. Is there -- are there any other matters to be raised? If not, we will resume tomorrow morning at 9.00. Yes, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm very happy for the interest in which -- that you, Mr. President, have shown in Jasmin Isic. I did up to yesterday make some inquiries about him, and I'm happy that you're of the same mind. I think, though, that there are certain mechanics or certain logistical procedure that would have to be put in place if either party or the Court will call him. So if the Court has expressed an interest in calling him - and it might well be something that will further our quest for the truth - then perhaps we could proceed from now to make inquiries as to -- to his whereabouts and what would be the best procedure to adopt to achieve what the Court has indicated might be in the interests of justice. So what I'm saying is that inquiry would have to be made as to the best methods to get him here. And if the Court wants him, we are prepared to assist in that regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Does the Defence have any comments? Very well. In that case, the hearing is adjourned and we will resume tomorrow at 9.00 in the morning. We have two witnesses scheduled for tomorrow, and I hope that they will both be present. So we will resume tomorrow at 9.00 with these two witnesses. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 23rd day of January, 2004, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 12.45 p.m.,
